title: Candidate experience best practices for recruiters
summary: Great candidate experience is fast, transparent, and respectful: clear next steps, real dates, visible status, and no logins or friction at any stage.

faq.q: What makes a good candidate experience?
faq.a: Speed, transparency, and respect: quick replies, clear next steps with real dates, no unnecessary logins, and honest communication regardless of the decision.

faq.q: How quickly should recruiters respond to candidates?
faq.a: Aim to acknowledge applications within a day or two and keep candidates updated at each stage. Silence is the most common candidate-experience complaint.

faq.q: How do you keep candidates informed between interview stages?
faq.a: Give every candidate a private status link showing their current stage, the next step, and an expected date, and nudge the recruiter internally whenever a candidate has gone too long without contact.

Most candidates will be rejected, so rejection is the experience most people have with your company. A prompt, kind, definitive no preserves the relationship and your employer brand; ghosting destroys both.
